standard.title: Synonyms and antonyms
standard.description: expand vocabulary by exploring a range of synonyms and antonyms, and using words encountered in a range of sources
standard.prior_knowledge: Students extend topic-specific vocabulary and understand that words can have different meanings in different contexts (AC9E3LA10). They have not yet explored synonyms and antonyms as vocabulary-expanding tools with shades of meaning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify synonyms and antonyms for words, explain how synonyms differ in shade of meaning, and apply new vocabulary from a range of sources — including First Nations Australian language words — in their own writing and discussion.

nodes.label: Synonyms and shades of meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify synonyms for a word and explain how synonyms differ in intensity, formality or connotation.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify two synonyms for a given word and explain one way they differ in meaning or use.
nodes.typical_width: Explore synonym clusters across a range of words (e.g. walk: stride, stroll, march, shuffle) and explain how the shades of meaning differ in intensity, formality and connotation, selecting the most precise synonym for specific contexts.
wider: Build synonym clusters for key vocabulary from a current cross-curriculum topic and compare shades of meaning to make precise choices in writing
Explore how synonyms can carry different cultural or emotional weights by examining words borrowed from First Nations Australian languages now used in Australian English

response_modes.reason: Synonym knowledge is accumulative — the richer the synonym repertoire, the more precise and varied a student's writing. This node rewards ongoing vocabulary collection across contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Synonym exploration — especially shades of meaning and connotation — is rich territory connecting vocabulary, style, audience and purpose. First Nations Australian language borrowings add significant cultural dimension.
success_criteria: Can name two synonyms for a given word and explain one difference in their meaning or connotation
Does not treat all synonyms as interchangeable — understands that word choice carries shade of meaning

nodes.label: Antonyms
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify antonyms and explain how antonym pairs help clarify meaning through contrast.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the antonym of a given word and explain how the contrast helps clarify meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Identify antonym pairs across a range of vocabulary domains and explain how antonyms are used in texts to create contrast, emphasise differences and clarify meaning.
wider: Examine how antonyms are used in persuasive texts to set up contrast between positions (e.g. safe vs dangerous, fair vs unfair)
Explore how antonym pairs shift across contexts — words that are antonyms in one context may not be in another
success_criteria: Can identify the antonym of a given word
Can explain how using an antonym pair in a sentence creates a contrast that clarifies meaning

nodes.label: Encountering and using new vocabulary
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use words encountered in reading and research — including technical, learning-area and First Nations Australian vocabulary — in their own spoken and written language.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two new vocabulary words encountered in a text or research task in their own writing or discussion, explaining the meaning of each.
nodes.typical_width: Deliberately collect and use new vocabulary from a range of sources — including subject-specific texts, research and texts by First Nations Australian authors — applying words in writing and discussion with attention to precision and appropriateness.
wider: Research words from First Nations Australian languages used in Australian English (e.g. place names, flora and fauna terms) and explore their origins and meanings
Create a personal vocabulary notebook organised by topic, collecting new words from cross-curriculum reading with definitions, synonyms and example sentences

response_modes.reason: Vocabulary expansion is fundamentally about accumulation. Students who encounter new words but do not use them do not retain them. Structured collection and active use across contexts builds lasting vocabulary range.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The breadth of vocabulary sources — subject texts, literature, First Nations Australian languages — is genuinely wide and significant. Active vocabulary collection is a high-value habit at this year level.
success_criteria: Can use a newly encountered word accurately in their own writing or speech
Can explain the meaning of the word and where they encountered it
